full_judgment:
8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed illegality and irregularity. He further submits that the findings and decision .of the appellate court is based on misreading and non-reading of evidences and non consideration of material facts, thereby affirmed the judgment passed by the trial court, which resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learning advocate also submits that, the trial court at the time of disposal of the original pre-emption case without proper assessment of evidence and without appreciation of law decided the merit of the case in favour of the pre-emptor, and the lower appellate court without assigning his independent reasons affirmed that judgment and order. The learned advocate submits that pursuant to the section 96(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all of the transferees shall be made parties. In the impugned registered deed of sale dated 23-2-2004 there are three transferees namely Md Ataur Rohman, Md Abdul Ahad and Md Layek Ahmed, though they have been impleaded as pre-emptees in the pre-emption case, but there were no valid Service of summons upon the pre-emptee No. 1 and 3 under Order V, rule 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, .as they live outside the country. Mr Tipu further submits that pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rahman lives permanently in UK with his family and no valid service of summons were made upon him at his address in UK at all, and that's why he could not contest in the case. Pre-emptor of the case neither substituted the legal heirs of the pre-emptee No. 1 after his death under Order 22 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure nor there were valid service summon under Order V Rule 25 and the trial court proceeded with the case in violation of the Code of Civil Procedure. The lower appellate court erred in law by relying on the Order XXII, rule 4(4) instead of the Order XXII, rule 4(1) and (3) as regards the substitution of the legal heirs of the pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rohman. Pre-emptee No. 3 Md Layek Ahmod lives in Saudi Arabia but it is admitted by the pre-emptor that no service of summons were made at his Saudi Arabia's address. A fraud practice was committed upon the court in the service of summons upon the pre-emptee No. 1 and 3. The PW 1 admitted during cross-examination that he did not take any steps for the substitution of the heirs of pre-emptee No. 1 namely Md Ataur Rohman who died in London, he also admitted that pre-emptee No. 3 lives in Saudi Arabia and he did not serve notice upon him at his address in Saudia Arabia. Learned counsel also submits that the question as to the service of summons were raised at in the written objection of the pre-emptee No. 2 at his earliest opportunity. Finally he submits that judgment and order of pre-emption obtained by suppressing summons is a judgment and order obtained fraudulently and, as such, nullity. In support of his submission he relied on the principles of law as set out in the decision reported in 12 BLC (AD) 79, 32 DLR (AD) 167, 2013 BLD (AD) 57 = 65 DLR (AD) 4 and 26 DLR 3. Accordingly, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and order suffers from material illegality and irregularity which deserves interference by this court. 

 9. On contrary learned Advocate Mr Md Nurul Amin for the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 controverting the arguments advanced from the learned advocate for the petitioner, and opposing the Rule by submitting that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal and deciding the merit of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned counsel further submits that the finding and decision of the appellate courts is based on proper appreciation of evidence on record. Learned counsel submits that the issue raised by the present petitioner that the pre-emption case is not maintainable as the legal heirs of the pre-emptee No. 1 Md Ataur Rahman were not substituted is not tenable in the eye of law because the pre-emptee No. 1 contested the case by filing the written statement but he did not contest the case anymore, and, as such, it is not necessary to substitute his legal heirs pursuant to Order 22 Rule 4(4) of the Civil Procedure Code. Learned counsel further submits that any objection as to omission of a necessary party must be taken at the earliest opportunity; if not so taken, may be deemed to have been waived. The pre-emption case cannot be failed for non joinder of parties. The pre-emptor prayed for supplying the foreign address of the pre-emptee No. 1 which was allowed by the trial court but the pre-emptee No. 2 failed to provide the address, and, as such, the pre-emptee No. 2 present petitioner is debarred from raising the point of defect of parties. The petitioner did not challenge the trial court's order No. 17 dated 5-6-2006 accepting the service of notice upon the pre-emptee No. 3 Md Layek Ahmed. Mr Md Nurul Amin for the opposite parties, in support of his submission referred to the decision 51 DLR 554, 31 DLR (AD) 88, 49 DLR (AD) 151, 12 MLR (AD) 120, 58 DLR (AD) 159 and 50 DLR 441.Finally he submits that the mere error of law is not ground for interfere in a revisional jurisdiction, unless the error of law caused occasioning failure of justice, accordingly he prays for discharge of the Rule.
